name: omniroute
description: Third-party local LLM gateway (OmniRoute), installed and pinned by hmd as a hardened fallback route for when the operator's normal provider quota is exhausted. Runs as a separate, operator-owned process bound to 127.0.0.1:20128 only. hmd's fallback policy gate (`bin/heimdall-fallback`) reads this module's state and decides whether to route to it; nothing about this module changes hmd's own traffic ambiently.
upstream_note: hmd vendors none of OmniRoute's code into this repository. One exact upstream commit is pinned and fetched fresh on install (see `pinned_version.pin_provenance`); hmd carries exactly one local patch on top of that pin (see `wires[0].detail` and `pinned_version.pin_provenance` for what it fixes and why).

pinned_version.pin_provenance: Verified by chain, not assumed. (1) GitHub API commit lookup for d82b68274c75c14d258b4898a34edc25d9712b87 in diegosouzapw/OmniRoute confirms the commit exists, dated 2026-08-25T02:46:45Z, message "fix(sse): exact-domain cookie match and origin-equality URL assertions (#11452)". (2) The exact tarball for that ref was fetched from codeload.github.com; GitHub's own content-disposition header names it OmniRoute-d82b68274c75c14d258b4898a34edc25d9712b87.tar.gz, recorded verbatim as this object's `artifact`. (3) `artifact_sha256` is a local SHA-256 (`shasum -a 256`) of that exact downloaded tarball, computed in two independent sessions with a byte-identical result: 370dfb82c6cd7faf98d81b581af6608080272b57cbf37cbbe8acb4b262e81818. (4) License was not inferred from repo-level metadata: the LICENSE file's content was fetched via the GitHub contents API at the pinned ref itself (?ref=d82b68274c75c14d258b4898a34edc25d9712b87) and decoded, confirming "MIT License / Copyright (c) 2026 diegosouzapw" text is genuinely present at this exact commit. Upstream is broken at this exact pin for a from-source build: wsPath.ts is missing resolveLiveWsUrl and sanitizeLiveWsPort, both of which upstream's own test file for that module already references -- the pinned commit does not build without them. hmd's local patch supplies both functions, verified against upstream's own test rather than invented behavior.

permission_class_note: Exactly one class applies. OmniRoute sits on the wire between hmd and a model provider whenever hmd's fallback gate routes to it -- the traffic-proxy class's own definition. The other three were checked and ruled out on their own terms, not skipped: storage-codec ("encodes or compresses data hmd writes to disk") does not apply -- OmniRoute stores nothing on hmd's behalf, it is a routing target, not a codec. tool-adapter ("wraps an external tool so hmd can drive it") does not apply -- hmd does not drive OmniRoute as a tool; it reads OmniRoute's own SQLite state read-only and calls it as an HTTP backend only when the fallback policy gate says so. rule-pack ("ships convention / stack-pack rules for the gate to apply") does not apply -- this module ships no gate rules. Declaring a second class here would overclaim; only traffic-proxy is real.
tier_note: No `tier_evidence` is claimed because none exists. `suggested` requires a pre-registered A/B receipt; nobody has run one for OmniRoute, so it stays at the floor tier (`available`) until somebody does.

installs_via.note: The fetch delegates to a dedicated script rather than a bare clone-and-untar one-liner because installing OmniRoute is real installation logic, not manifest data: it has to build from source (node v24.13.0 required, OMNIROUTE_USE_TURBOPACK=0), apply hmd's local wsPath.ts patch on top of the pinned commit before that build, place the checkout and its data directory at fixed paths (/Users/rj/omniroute, ~/.omniroute), rotate the management password off its shipped default, and start the loopback-only listener. `bin/heimdall-omniroute-install` takes no required arguments, runs non-interactively, and exits non-zero on any failure -- wrong node version, the patch failing to apply, the build failing, or the port already being held by something else.

wires.detail: Not a literal `hmd wrap <tool>` CLI chain -- OmniRoute is reached through hmd's fallback policy gate, not a wrapped command. `bin/heimdall-fallback` is the chain hmd actually offers to reach this module: a read-only policy gate that reads OmniRoute's SQLite state and decides a verdict plus config, and never calls OmniRoute directly itself. The generic HTTP transport that eventually carries the traffic (`bin/hmd-exec`, `bin/lib/hmd_api_backend.py`) is deliberately not the wire target: by design it holds zero references to OmniRoute (grep-confirmed at manifest authoring time) because it is provider-agnostic and only consumes whatever config `bin/heimdall-fallback` hands it. Wiring to the generic transport would measure ROUTED=0 for a module that is, in fact, wired, and misreport it as unwired.

loopback-only-bind.command:
set -u
out="$(lsof -nP -iTCP:20128 -sTCP:LISTEN 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR>1')"
if [ -z "$out" ]; then
  echo 'NON_VERIFIED no listener on :20128 -- an unreachable check fails, never passes'
  exit 1
fi
if printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq '(\*|0\.0\.0\.0|::):20128'; then
  echo 'NON-LOOPBACK-BIND-DETECTED'
  exit 1
fi
if printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q '127\.0\.0\.1:20128'; then
  echo 'LOOPBACK-ONLY-OK'
else
  echo 'NON_VERIFIED listener present but address unrecognized'
  exit 1
fi
loopback-only-bind.why: OmniRoute must never be reachable off-box. A bind to 0.0.0.0 or :: turns a local convenience into a network-exposed credential store. Checked by asking the OS which address the live listener on :20128 actually holds, not by trusting configuration that claims loopback-only.

management-password-rotated.why: The management plane is root credential for every provider connection OmniRoute holds. If the shipped default password still authenticates, anyone who can reach the port owns every credential inside. Checked by attempting the literal shipped default against the live login endpoint and requiring it be rejected.

secret-files-0600.command:
set -u
dir="$HOME/.omniroute"
if [ ! -d "$dir" ]; then
  echo "NON_VERIFIED $dir does not exist -- an unreachable check fails, never passes"
  exit 1
fi
files="$(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -iname '*env*' -o -iname '*password*' -o -iname '*.key' -o -iname '*secret*' -o -iname '*credential*' \) 2>/dev/null)"
if [ -z "$files" ]; then
  echo "NON_VERIFIED no secret-shaped files found under $dir -- an unreachable check fails, never passes"
  exit 1
fi
bad=""
count=0
while IFS= read -r f; do
  [ -n "$f" ] || continue
  count=$((count+1))
  perm="$(stat -f '%Lp' "$f" 2>/dev/null || stat -c '%a' "$f" 2>/dev/null)"
  if [ "$perm" != "600" ]; then
    bad="$bad $f(mode=$perm)"
  fi
done <<EOF
$files
EOF
if [ -n "$bad" ]; then
  echo "BAD-PERMS$bad"
  exit 1
fi
echo "SECRETS-0600-OK checked=$count"
secret-files-0600.why: OmniRoute's on-disk secrets are only as private as their file mode. Checked by globbing every secret-shaped filename actually present under ~/.omniroute and requiring each be exactly 600 -- not just the files this manifest happens to name, so a renamed or newly added secret file cannot silently escape the check.

tier1-credential-absent.command:
set -u
db="$HOME/.omniroute/storage.sqlite"
if [ ! -e "$db" ]; then
  echo "NON_VERIFIED $db does not exist -- an unreachable check fails, never passes"
  exit 1
fi
if ! command -v sqlite3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo 'NON_VERIFIED sqlite3 not available -- an unreachable check fails, never passes'
  exit 1
fi
rows="$(sqlite3 -readonly "$db" \
  "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM provider_connections WHERE provider IN ('claude','claude-web');" 2>/dev/null)"
if [ -z "$rows" ]; then
  echo "NON_VERIFIED query against $db failed -- an unreachable check fails, never passes"
  exit 1
fi
if [ "$rows" = "0" ]; then
  echo "TIER1-CREDENTIAL-ABSENT-OK rows=$rows"
else
  echo "TIER1-CREDENTIAL-PRESENT rows=$rows -- Tier-1 mitigation is DEFEATED"
  exit 1
fi
tier1-credential-absent.why: hmd's Tier-1 mitigation (a Claude Code subscription cannot be repurposed as a routing backend) is not a setting -- it is the empirical absence of a `provider_connections` row for `claude`/`claude-web`. Checked by querying OmniRoute's own SQLite state directly, read-only, for that exact row.

non-interactive-passthrough.command:
set -u
a="$(bin/heimdall-fallback check </dev/null 2>/dev/null | cat)"
DEAD="http://127.0.0.1:9"
b="$(env HTTP_PROXY="$DEAD" HTTPS_PROXY="$DEAD" ALL_PROXY="$DEAD" http_proxy="$DEAD" https_proxy="$DEAD" all_proxy="$DEAD" bin/heimdall-fallback check </dev/null 2>/dev/null | cat)"
if [ -z "$a" ]; then
  echo 'NON_VERIFIED bin/heimdall-fallback check produced no output -- an unreachable check fails, never passes'
  exit 1
fi
if [ "$a" = "$b" ]; then
  echo 'PASSTHROUGH-OK'
else
  echo "PASSTHROUGH-DIVERGED -- ambient proxy vars changed heimdall-fallback's non-interactive output"
  exit 1
fi
non-interactive-passthrough.why: A traffic-proxy module must not change hmd's own behaviour merely by existing in the environment. Checked by diffing `bin/heimdall-fallback check`'s non-interactive output with and without ambient proxy variables pointed at a dead address -- they must be byte-identical.

no-signed-traffic-routing.command:
set -u
wired=0
for f in bin/heimdall-presence bin/heimdall-connect bin/heimdall-team; do
  if [ ! -f "$f" ]; then
    echo "NON_VERIFIED $f does not exist -- an unreachable check fails, never passes"
    exit 1
  fi
  if grep -qiE 'hmd-exec|hmd_api_backend|heimdall-fallback|127\.0\.0\.1:20128' "$f"; then
    wired=$((wired+1))
  fi
done
if [ "$wired" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "SIGNED-SURFACE-REFERENCES-OMNIROUTE count=$wired"
  exit 1
fi

. bin/lib/cp-consent.sh
. bin/lib/hmd-gate-endpoint.sh
CP="${HEIMDALL_DEFAULT_CP_URL%/}"
POISON="http://127.0.0.1:20128"
clean="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 15 "$CP/readyz" 2>/dev/null)"; [ -n "$clean" ] || clean=000
if [ "$clean" != "200" ]; then
  echo "NON_VERIFIED control-plane unreachable (clean probe -> $clean) -- an unreachable check fails, never passes"
  exit 1
fi
signed="$(CP_PROBE="$CP" ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="$POISON" HTTP_PROXY="$POISON" HTTPS_PROXY="$POISON" ALL_PROXY="$POISON" hmd_signed_exec sh -c 'curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 15 "$CP_PROBE/readyz"' 2>/dev/null)"
[ -n "$signed" ] || signed=000
if [ "$signed" = "200" ]; then
  echo "SIGNED-BYPASS-OK static_refs=$wired poisoned_base_url_signed=$signed"
else
  echo "SIGNED-ROUTED-OR-BROKEN static_refs=$wired poisoned_base_url_signed=$signed"
  exit 1
fi
no-signed-traffic-routing.why: hmd's signed control-plane calls must never be silently rerouted through a proxy module, OmniRoute or otherwise. Checked two ways: hmd_signed_exec must still reach the real control plane even when ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL/HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY are poisoned to OmniRoute's own loopback port, proving the signed path scrubs them; and a static grep confirms none of hmd's three signed-traffic surfaces (heimdall-presence, heimdall-connect, heimdall-team) reference OmniRoute's transport at all.

consent_waived_reason: Not waived, unlike headroom. Headroom's waiver rests on a maintainer default-inclusion decision (`default_included: true`) for a module whose worst case is a storage/traffic wrapper hmd already constrains tightly. OmniRoute is `default_included: false`, holds live provider credentials behind its own management plane, and its Tier-1 mitigation depends on an absence (no `claude`/`claude-web` row) that a management-plane compromise could violate after install -- a risk shape headroom's waiver reasoning does not cover. So every install prints `consent_text` and requires an explicit yes; there is no distribution decision here that justifies skipping it.
consent_text:
OmniRoute is a third-party LLM gateway that hmd can install locally as a hardened fallback route for when your normal provider quota is exhausted. It is not part of hmd's own code -- hmd fetches, pins, and runs an upstream project (https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute) as a separate, operator-owned process on this machine, bound to 127.0.0.1:20128 only. It is never installed by default; you are seeing this because you (or something acting for you) asked to add it.

What it holds: OmniRoute stores real provider API keys/connections and has its own management web plane. That management plane is effectively a root credential for everything OmniRoute touches -- it can add, remove, or read back provider connections, change settings, and export or import its entire database. Anyone who can authenticate to it can do anything OmniRoute itself can do.

The risk that matters most (Tier-1): hmd relies on OmniRoute's `provider_connections` table holding no row for `claude` or `claude-web`, because a live Claude Code subscription with a row in that table could be reused as a routing backend -- a mitigation hmd depends on structurally, not by policy. `blockedProviders` is visibility-only and is not a kill switch. At install time, the installer rotates OmniRoute's management password off its shipped default and verifies no such row exists before anything is wired up. But nothing afterward structurally prevents someone who later obtains the (by-then rotated) management password from adding a `claude` or `claude-web` connection through OmniRoute's own UI -- the absence is enforced at install time, and re-checked by this manifest's `tier1-credential-absent` invariant whenever hmd re-validates this module, not continuously in real time by OmniRoute itself. Keeping the management password secret is what keeps this mitigation real between checks.

A second, related residual risk: OmniRoute's own web layer does not allowlist the Host header, so it is theoretically exposed to DNS-rebinding-style attacks that trick a browser into treating it as same-origin. This is upstream's own gap; hmd's patch does not touch it. Exploiting it in practice still requires acting as an authenticated session against the management plane, so it is gated on the same password secrecy described above -- but the structural gap itself is real, is upstream's, and remains regardless of how well the password is kept.

What hmd changed, and why: hmd vendors none of OmniRoute's code -- it fetches and pins one exact upstream commit (see `pinned_version`) and carries exactly one local patch on top: at the pinned commit, upstream's own wsPath.ts is missing resolveLiveWsUrl and sanitizeLiveWsPort, functions upstream's own test file for that module already expects -- the pinned commit does not build without them. hmd's patch supplies both and was verified against upstream's own test, not invented behavior papering over a build error.

Disk footprint: have at least 16 GB free before installing -- that is a safety margin, not the durable cost. A fresh build's peak transient usage is dependencies (about 3.3 GB, deterministic from the lockfile) plus build output split between an unused build variant this deployment doesn't run and the production output it does (together about 1.3 GB) plus one generation of Next.js's build-time compiler cache, whose exact single-build size varies with codebase size and could not be pinned down precisely without risking a live install -- bounded above by roughly 9 GB observed on a machine with several days of accumulated builds. This installer's automatic post-build cleanup then removes the unused build variant and the compiler cache, bringing the durable footprint down to roughly 3.6 GB. See docs/analysis/2026-08-29-omniroute-disk-footprint.md for the full measured breakdown, including what was and wasn't verified. Separately: if OmniRoute's browser-automation feature is ever exercised, Playwright downloads its own browser binaries on demand (roughly 500 MB, cached outside this install and shared with any other project on the machine using a compatible Playwright version) -- this installer never triggers that download itself.

Reversible: `hmd modules remove omniroute` stops the local process and removes the installed copy and its data directory. hmd's own repository carries none of OmniRoute's code, so nothing of it remains in this codebase either way.

Declining is a normal, supported outcome. If you say no, hmd's fallback behaviour stays exactly what it was before this module existed.
